title: Per-tool sizing for MCP tools that routinely produce over-cap responses
wanted_capability: Tools that routinely emit >80KB responses should size their output at the producer (pagination, filters, tail/limit params, structured-result accessors) instead of relying on the blanket MCP response cap. The cap is now lossless (over-cap payloads spill to <state_dir>/response-dumps/ with a spilled_to pointer in the envelope, src/server/response.rs), but a spill is still a failure of the producing tool's shaping: programmatic consumers (code-mode isolates, JS workflow scripts) get an indirection instead of data, and interactive agents burn a turn on file reads. Wanted: identify chronic over-producers from the per-call bytes field already logged at blackbox::tool (journalctl --user -u blackbox | grep bbox_), and give each a proper paginated/filtered variant. Known instance: bro_wait's ~81k multi-escaped result envelope (gap-55be3518).
missing_primitive: Per-tool response shaping (pagination/limit/filter params) on chronic over-cap producers; observability query for which tools trip the cap most
fallback_used: Made the blanket cap lossless via spill-to-disk (response-dumps + spilled_to path) so over-cap responses are recoverable instead of destroyed
resolution_note: obsolete: 8ccdcd06 replaced the spill-to-disk cap with a typed producer error (error.response_too_large with a per-tool hint and a blackbox::tool response_too_large warn carrying tool and bytes, src/server/response.rs::bounded_response), so over-cap output is no longer an implicit export. The known chronic producers now shape their own output: bro_wait structured results (gap-55be3518, bro_arc_result), bbox_thread get detail views and paged body (src/tools/threads.rs), bro_brofile list/get summary and body pages (src/tools/roster.rs), bbox_storage_health file pages (src/tools/storage_health.rs), and bbox_storage_gc detail cursor (src/tools/storage_gc.rs), each with under-cap tests. A newly identified over-producer should be filed as its own gap naming the tool.
